# Your income can affect it
## on this page
- [Family income](https://www.servicesaustralia.gov.au/your-income-can-affect-child-care-subsidy?context=41186#familyincomeccs)
- [Withholding](https://www.servicesaustralia.gov.au/your-income-can-affect-child-care-subsidy?context=41186#withholdingccs)

## Family income
Your CCS percentage applies to either your [hourly fee](https://www.servicesaustralia.gov.au/type-child-care-you-use-can-affect-child-care-subsidy?context=41186#hourlyfee) or the relevant [hourly rate cap](https://www.servicesaustralia.gov.au/type-child-care-you-use-can-affect-child-care-subsidy?context=41186#hourlyrate), whichever is lower.

We pay this directly to your child care service to reduce the fees you pay.

Use the [Child Care Subsidy calculator](https://www.startingblocks.gov.au/child-care-subsidy-calculator) on the Starting Blocks website to see what you may be eligible for.

### Standard CCS rates
If you have more than one child aged 5 or younger, you may get a [higher rate](https://www.servicesaustralia.gov.au/your-number-children-care-can-affect-your-higher-child-care-subsidy?context=41186#who) for one or more of your children.

We’ll do this when we [balance your payments](https://www.servicesaustralia.gov.au/balancing-child-care-subsidy?context=41186) at the end of the financial year.

Child Care Subsidy Income estimate - YouTube

[Child Care Subsidy Income estimate](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=2AgLUdh9nOw) [Services Australia](https://www.youtube.com/channel/UCg5fHRiVL9fvAgQ-OP2FyHw)

[Watch on](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=2AgLUdh9nOw)

[Transcript](https://www.servicesaustralia.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-04/transcript-child-care-subsidy-income-estimate.docx)

## Withholding
If you’d like to change it more often than this, call the [Families line](https://www.servicesaustralia.gov.au/your-income-can-affect-child-care-subsidy?context=41186#toolbar-phone).

We use your family income estimate to work out how much subsidy you’ll get. This means at the end of each financial year, we’ll [balance your payment](https://www.servicesaustralia.gov.au/balancing-child-care-subsidy?context=41186) using your [actual adjusted taxable income](https://www.servicesaustralia.gov.au/what-adjusted-taxable-income?context=41186). We compare this information to make sure we’ve subsidised your child care fees correctly in the financial year.

You can also use the [Express Plus Centrelink mobile app](https://www.servicesaustralia.gov.au/express-plus-centrelink-mobile-app).

If you overestimated your family income and didn’t get enough subsidy, we’ll pay any outstanding amount directly to you.

# A guide to Australian Government payments
## 20 September 2026 to 31 December 2026
### Family Tax Benefit Part A
Family Tax Benefit Part A is a supplementary payment to assist low and middle income families with the direct costs of raising dependent children. It is paid for each eligible child in the family and can be paid in fortnightly instalments or as an annual lump sum.

For more information, go to **servicesaustralia.gov.au/ftb** or call us on the Families line (page 60).

##### Supplementary support
| Payments | Available to: |
|-|-|
| Parental Leave Pay (page 10) | recipients with a newborn or newly adopted child. |
| Newborn Supplement and Newborn Upfront Payment (page 4) | recipients with a newborn or newly adopted child. |
| Parenting Payment (page 12) | recipients with principal care of a young child. |
| Child Care Subsidy (page 7) | recipients with a child in approved child care. |

For more information about payments and services based on individual circumstances, go to **servicesaustralia.gov.au/paymentfinder**

###### Family Tax Benefit advance
Families may also be able to access a lump sum Family Tax Benefit advance if their fortnightly rate of Family Tax Benefit Part A is at least the base rate for one child, and if repayment of the advance will not cause them to suffer financial hardship. Up to 7.5% of a family’s annual Family Tax Benefit Part A entitlement may be paid in advance at any one time, up to a $1,430.46 limit.

web.description:
## Phone us
### Centrelink families line
Use this line if you need help with family payments, such as Family Tax Benefit, Child Care Subsidy, Parental Leave Pay, Foster Child Health Care Card.

[136 150](tel:136150)

[Listen](https://app-oc.readspeaker.com/cgi-bin/rsent?customerid=5525&lang=en_au&readid=content&readclass=lit-readspeaker-target&url=https%3A//www.servicesaustralia.gov.au/balancing-child-care-subsidy%3Fcontext%3D41186)

# Balancing Child Care Subsidy
## on this page
- [If you lodge a tax return](https://www.servicesaustralia.gov.au/balancing-child-care-subsidy?context=41186#ifyoulodge)
- [If you got Family Tax Benefit (FTB)](https://www.servicesaustralia.gov.au/balancing-child-care-subsidy?context=41186#ifyougotftb)

## If you don’t need to lodge a tax return
You must include all [adjusted taxable income](https://www.servicesaustralia.gov.au/what-adjusted-taxable-income?context=41186) you got from Centrelink and any other income you had.

## If you got Family Tax Benefit (FTB)
It’s important to know we balance FTB and CCS separately. If you got CCS, you’ll need to confirm your income, even if you don’t need to for FTB.

If we’ve balanced your FTB based on your tax return details, we’ll use this information to balance your CCS.

If you’ve told us that you don’t need to lodge a tax return and confirmed your income, we’ll use this information to balance your CCS.

Find out more about [balancing FTB](https://www.servicesaustralia.gov.au/balancing-family-tax-benefit).

[When we balance your Child Care Subsidy\
\
We balance Child Care Subsidy (CCS) from mid-August.](https://www.servicesaustralia.gov.au/when-we-balance-your-child-care-subsidy?context=41186)

[Understanding your Child Care Subsidy balancing outcome\
\
Once we’ve balanced your Child Care Subsidy (CCS), we’ll let you know the outcome in writing.](https://www.servicesaustralia.gov.au/understanding-your-child-care-subsidy-balancing-outcome?context=41186)
